findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile 06e0's pyproject.toml ratchet flip with the parent's explicit exclusion of that flip and with 879f's 'pyproject.toml comment-lines-only, exactly-4-files' diff ACs (sequence/merge order or confirm 06e0 is not a child of this epic).
evidence: Parent Scope selection: 'Deliberately EXCLUDED: ... The typing ratchet FLIP in pyproject.toml (contended x9)'

06e0 AC: 'pyproject.toml lists them in the disallow_untyped_defs override (2 before, 13 after)' and 'A second [[tool.mypy.overrides]] block sets disallow_any_explicit = true' — i.e. real key/value additions to pyproject.toml
879f AC: 'git diff pyproject.toml shows comment lines only (no key/value change)' and 'git diff --name-only origin/main lists exactly README.md, docs/README.md, docs/user-guide.md, pyproject.toml'
findings.finding: Sibling 06e0 performs the pyproject.toml typing-ratchet FLIP that the parent plan's Scope-selection explicitly EXCLUDES, and it edits pyproject.toml concurrently with sibling 879f, which asserts its diff is 'exactly README.md, docs/README.md, docs/user-guide.md, pyproject.toml' with 'comment lines only (no key/value change).'
scenarios: Both 06e0 and 879f land against the same pyproject.toml; 879f's diff-scope AC ('comment lines only') is verified against a pyproject.toml that 06e0 has already given real override blocks, or the two changes race and one rebases the other.
findings.suggested_fix: State an explicit ordering (879f lands first, then 06e0) and note in 06e0 that it supersedes the parent's 'excluded' status once contention clears; or confirm 06e0 belongs to a different epic and remove it from this parent's coverage set.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile 5e53's near-cap CI-gate warning and repo-wide module-size draining with the parent's explicit deferral of that CI/enforcement work to a separate out-of-scope proposal (confirm 5e53's parent, or update the parent's scope narrative).
evidence: Parent 'Recommended systemic follow-up (out of scope here)': the early-warning margin 'changes enforcement policy and touches the (contended) gate/CI config, so it belongs in its own proposal, not these non-overlapping stories.'

5e53 Change 3: 'Append to that same [Module-size gate] step a NON-BLOCKING pass emitting one ::warning:: ... One edit: the gate lives only in the reusable _build-and-test.yml, which both gerrit-verify.yaml and test.yml call.'
5e53 also drains near-cap files pass1.py/push.py which the parent lists among excluded contended near-cap files.
findings.finding: Sibling 5e53 does repo-wide module-size draining plus a CI module-size-gate change (a near-cap ::warning:: pass edited into the reusable _build-and-test.yml) — work the parent's Scope-selection excludes ('near-cap files ... all contended') and defers to a separate proposal ('Recommended systemic follow-up ... touches the (contended) gate/CI config, so it belongs in its own proposal, not these non-overlapping stories').
scenarios: 5e53 edits the reusable CI workflow file that the parent designated as belonging to a separate, out-of-scope proposal; the epic's 'every NEW child touches only zero-contention files' invariant (parent Scope selection) is undercut by a sibling touching CI config.
findings.suggested_fix: Either move 5e53 under the separate systemic-follow-up proposal the parent references, or amend the parent's Scope/Recommended-follow-up sections to acknowledge 5e53 as the in-epic vehicle for the near-cap warning.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC1 with fade-ea90's `duplicate` closure: credit the actual durable fix (2207-2917-e21b-42bd / commit 8c9bf5d78d, CPython 86296 asyncio.timeout) as the resolution, and either scope-in or explicitly track the still-live load-dependent xdist teardown-channel race (OSError: cannot send) reported on fade-ea90 rather than asserting the worker 'no longer dies'.
evidence: fade-ea90 closed with class `duplicate` of 2207-2917-e21b-42bd; its re-measurement states 'the plan's root-cause hypothesis was falsified before this ticket was written' and 'ACs 1-3 encode the app-owned-ThreadPoolExecutor hypothesis ... 2207's RCA investigated and explicitly rejected that hypothesis'.

Proven mechanism per 2207 RCA: 'CPython issue 86296: on Python 3.11, asyncio.wait_for consumes an external cancellation ... 8c9bf5d78d replaced asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.to_thread(...)) with async with asyncio.timeout(...)'.

fade-ea90 comment (2026-08-13): 'load-dependent worker-channel teardown race ... two full-suite runs died in xdist teardown with OSError: cannot send (already closed?)' — a distinct, still-reproducible flake in the same symptom class.
The epic marks AC1 [x] without noting that the adopted child's mechanism was disproven or that a residual teardown-race flake remains.
findings.finding: AC1 adopts fade-ea90 as the resolution vehicle for the CI xdist flake, but fade-ea90's root-cause hypothesis (app-owned ThreadPoolExecutor) was falsified and it closed as `duplicate`; the actual durable fix (CPython 86296 / asyncio.timeout, commit 8c9bf5d78d) lives in a different ticket, and a distinct teardown-channel-race flake may still be live.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, line 1 ('CI flake fade-ea90 resolved ... so the Python 3.11 xdist worker no longer dies in test_opcert_service_app'); Children ('Adopted existing open tickets: fade-ea90-7564-4715 (CI flake bug)')
scenarios: A reader/implementer treats AC1 as satisfied by fade-ea90's proposed executor change, which the RCA shows does not fix the py3.11 crash.
The py3.11 (or load-dependent teardown) worker death recurs after the epic is marked complete because the named child does not address the proven cause.
